key_insight: Benign-looking fine-tuning data can erode LLM safety, and gradient alignment can help identify and filter examples linked to unsafe behavior.
engineering_relevance: SimpleLoRIF makes gradient-based safety filtering practical for million-example post-training datasets while largely preserving model capabilities.
method: Compute low-rank gradient embeddings with backpropagation restricted to the final four transformer blocks.
Rank training examples by gradient alignment with unsafe responses.
Create SafeTulu by removing the 20% most aligned examples from Tulu 3.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports emergent-misalignment attribution AUC up to 0.865 and GCG attack success rate reductions up to 22% across Qwen, Llama, and Olmo, outperforming judge-based and prior gradient-based filtering.
watch_item: Filtering depends on the unsafe-response signals used for alignment; improvements on GCG attacks do not establish protection against all unsafe behaviors.
paper_title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
